clue.text: Put away drink after drive

indicators.note: drink comes after drive, so its letters follow in the answer

parts.note: to send is to drive, as in sending someone mad
to down a pint is to drink it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to finish their drink once they've finished driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' looks like drinking up, but here it means locking someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who sends someone down puts them away in prison, an informal British idiom.

clue.text: Cover of magazine turned over, after sex article

indicators.note: the reversed cover comes after the word for sex

parts.note: IT is old slang for sex appeal or sex itself

indicators.note: turned over says those two letters are read the other way round
the cover of a word is its outside, the letters at either end of magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine's cover story about sex, flipped over to show the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single piece in a newspaper or list, the same as an article.

clue.text: Python, perhaps, welcomes second TV series

parts.note: a hi is a greeting, so welcomes can be his
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: A snake documentary greets a second season on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' reads as a verb but is the plural noun: greetings, hi's.
explanation.definitionFit: A python is a snake, and snakes hiss, so it is an example of a hissing creature.

clue.text: Pole position at the start, drink put on ice

parts.note: a pole is an upright post

indicators.note: at the start picks the opening letter of position

parts.note: one is a drink, as in 'one for the road'

explanation.surface: Racing on pole position, then a drink is chilled on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something on ice is an idiom for delaying it, to defer it to a later date.

clue.text: Lies lead to Farage, as reality gets distorted

indicators.note: the lead to a word is its first letter, here of Farage
something distorted is twisted out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A political jab: falsehoods steer Nigel Farage while reality is bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales are invented, untrue stories, so the phrase is an idiom for falsehoods.

clue.text: Brown from swimming in sea around noon

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the letter for noon
swimming suggests letters moving about, so in sea is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sun tan acquired from swimming in the sea at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' makes SIENA from IN SEA; 'around' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy pigment, a reddish or yellowish brown shade used by painters.

clue.text: Mount finest horse

parts.note: the finest is the best
a ride is a horse to ride, a mount

explanation.surface: A jockey is told to get on the finest horse in the stable.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to sit astride something, so to climb on as you would a saddle.

clue.text: Bishop in file at the back by a rook getting check

indicators.note: at the back takes the final letter of file

parts.note: by as in multiplied by is the times sign X
R is the chess abbreviation for rook
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A chess game: a bishop in the rear file, next to a rook, gives check.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: the bishop is a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An exarch is a senior prelate in the Eastern Orthodox church, ranking above a bishop.

clue.text: Plant kiss on round lips, softly going to hug one

indicators.note: to hug is to enclose, so the rest wraps round the letter for one
kiss goes on round, after it in an across answer

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: going says the letter for softly leaves lips

parts.note: P is the musical direction piano, softly
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A romantic gesture: a gentle kiss on round lips, then a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hug' encloses the A with everything else, so it lands between the kiss and the trimmed lips rather than inside the lips alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxalis is a genus of plants, the wood sorrels, with clover-like leaves.

clue.text: Second person to try Apple iPad, a man's content

indicators.note: content as a noun is what something holds, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone testing an Apple iPad, and a man's contentment with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam is usually 'first person'; in Genesis Eve ate the apple first, so he was the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Eden story Eve took the forbidden fruit and then gave it to her husband.

clue.text: Bit of trouble cutting grass

indicators.note: cutting into a word means splitting it and going inside

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing, which is also to sing
what's the matter means what's the trouble

explanation.surface: A spot of bother while mowing the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like a lawn but is the verb for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small amount, a scattering of something.

clue.text: Make love with fellow: let me see thing

parts.note: to make is to do, as in doing a drawing
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
er is the hesitation noise of someone thinking it over

explanation.surface: An awkward romantic proposal, with a pause to think it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make love' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A doofer is informal British slang for any object whose name you can't recall, a whatsit.

clue.text: Following match on ground where captain might be

parts.note: a match gives a light
the deck is the ground, as in hit the deck

explanation.surface: A cricket captain after the match, out on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting picture misleads: the captain flies a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's pilot in command sits up front in the cockpit, also called the flight deck.

clue.text: National horse is short, can it hit fences?

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the rearranged letters surround the shortened horse
hit as in hard hit, damaged, so can it is rearranged
is short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed coat

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a short horse can clear the fences at the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is short' trims ROAN to ROA; 'hit' makes CTIAN from CAN IT, which 'fences' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a citizen of Croatia, someone of that nationality.

clue.text: Sounds hooters, the first person must go inside

indicators.note: must go inside says the pronoun is placed within the slang word for hooters

parts.note: hooters is slang for noses
the first person pronoun is I

explanation.surface: Car horns blaring, and someone insists on going in first.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds, especially loud or unwelcome ones.

clue.text: Rash of the skin, not initially red

indicators.note: not says that letter is left out

parts.note: epidermic means relating to the epidermis, the outer skin

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of red

explanation.surface: A medical note: a skin rash that isn't red at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The skin picture misleads: 'Rash' is an outbreak, not a spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash of something is a sudden spate of it, and an epidemic is a widespread outbreak.

clue.text: Chaos from British far-right group before noon

parts.note: the EDL is the English Defence League, a British far-right street movement
am, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A morning march by a British extremist group causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from London's old Bethlem asylum, means uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Snowball in face, fell over

parts.note: mush is British slang for a face

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a fell is a northern English hill or upland moor

explanation.surface: Hit in the face by a snowball and knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' is not the verb but a noun for moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: To snowball is to grow rapidly, the same verb sense as to spring up and expand quickly.

clue.text: A barrel, say, runs out when filling beer container

indicators.note: filling means going inside, here into beer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: runs out says those two letters leave the word for barrel

parts.note: a keg is a small barrel
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A barrel of beer has run out while being poured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a passing comment but is EG, taken out of KEG to leave K.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a drinking cup or lab vessel, a kind of open vessel.

clue.text: Jade and tire, hen party's starting to get drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters are rearranged
starting takes the opening letter of party's

explanation.surface: A tired woman on a hen party who starts drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jade' and 'tire' look like a pair meaning weary, but Jade is the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephrite is one of the two minerals sold as jade, the other being jadeite.

clue.text: Periods of quiet — manage to get upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Periods of silence, struggling to cope and getting upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochs are eras, long spans of history.

clue.text: Neglect daughter, one son gets help

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to be of use is to be of help

explanation.surface: A parent ignores their daughter while their son gets support.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of being unused, left to fall into neglect.

clue.text: Take an empty elevator to go down for reception

indicators.note: reception means taking in, so the dive letters receive the others

parts.note: to dive is to go down

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving the outer letters of elevator

explanation.surface: Riding an empty lift down to the hotel reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reception' looks like a hotel lobby but means taking in.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to obtain or get it from a source.

clue.text: Club member getting birdie?

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club
pecker is slang for the male member

explanation.surface: A golf club member scores a birdie, one under par.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture misleads: 'birdie' is just a small bird, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodpecker is a bird, and birdie is a childish word for any small bird.

clue.text: Soldiers stand around for drill

indicators.note: around says the word for stand goes round the soldiers

parts.note: to stand is to be, as in let it be
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand about on the parade ground waiting for drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' looks like parade-ground practice but is the verb to bore a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore is to make a hole with a tool, the same as drilling.

clue.text: Broke, mostly get by begging on street

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to bum is to cadge, getting things by begging

explanation.surface: Penniless, mostly getting by from begging on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust is informal for bankrupt, having no money left.

clue.text: Switzerland and Italy twice affected

indicators.note: twice says the pair of codes is written two times

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Switzerland and Italy are both hit by something, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi means showy or pretentious, fussily elegant.

clue.text: Studying for an exam about conception

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a conception is an idea, a vision

explanation.surface: Cramming for a test on the topic of conception.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, revision is the usual word for going over material before a test.
